title: GHz-rate all-fiber active polarization state analyzer for quantum protocols
authors: Andrea Pompermaier, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Giuseppe Vallone, Paolo Villoresi
abstract: Active selection of the measurement basis underpins quantum protocols including device-independent quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation with active feed-forward, and Bell tests. High-speed operation is crucial to minimize the latency between consecutive measurement choices, enabling faster protocol execution and higher achievable communication rates. Here, we demonstrate a GHz-rate all-fiber polarization state analyzer enabling active, trial-by-trial reconfiguration of the measurement basis, which we validate by performing a CHSH Bell test. The state analyzer is based on a fiber Sagnac interferometer incorporating a lithium niobate electro-optic phase modulator, built entirely using off-the-shelf fiber-optic components. Operating at a nominal repetition rate of 1 GHz, the system performs dynamic polarization measurements for the CHSH Bell test, achieving polarization visibilities up to 99% and a violation of $S = 2.6975 \pm 0.0005$, certifying entanglement at an unprecedented rate. Furthermore, the system demonstrates excellent long-term stability, preserving the Bell-inequality violation for more than 6 hours without realignment. These results establish the proposed state analyzer as a versatile, scalable platform for quantum communication protocols requiring fast, reconfigurable polarization-state measurements.
summary: The paper introduces a novel, all-fiber active polarization state analyzer capable of operating at 1 GHz. By integrating lithium niobate EOMs into a Sagnac interferometer, the device enables rapid, trial-by-trial reconfiguration of measurement bases. This achievement validates its use in high-rate quantum protocols by successfully performing a CHSH Bell test with high fidelity and long-term stability.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a high-speed, actively reconfigurable polarization state analyzer necessary for executing advanced quantum protocols like device-independent QKD or Bell tests.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a functional all-fiber analyzer capable of performing dynamic polarization measurements at a record rate of 1 GHz while maintaining high entanglement fidelity ($S = 2.6975 \pm 0.0005$).
method: The system utilizes an entangled photon source and analyzes the polarization state using a Sagnac interferometer incorporating a lithium niobate electro-optic phase modulator (EOM).
model_or_system: The platform is entirely fiber-based, employing off-the-shelf components to achieve active basis selection. The measurement process involves calculating effective projectors based on the total unitary transformation applied by the Sagnac loop and EOM.
key_observables: Polarization visibilities (up to 99%); CHSH Bell parameter violation ($S = 2.6975 \pm 0.0005$); Long-term stability of entanglement violation over $>6$ hours.
important_parameters: Nominal repetition rate of $1	ext{ GHz}$; Low operating voltage required for LiNbO$_3$ EOMs compared to bulk cells.
main_assumptions: The primary practical limitation noted is the insertion loss (2–4 dB) associated with coupling commercial LiNbO$_3$ EOMs to optical fibers.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the schematic of the analyzer components. Figure 2 illustrates the experimental setup using a fiber-based source generating entangled pairs at 1 GHz for Alice and Bob receivers.
paper_structure: The paper details the necessity of fast basis selection, presents the physical realization using Sagnac interferometers and EOMs, validates the system performance via a high-rate CHSH Bell test, and discusses future improvements to mitigate coupling losses.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in quantum communication by providing a robust, scalable platform for fast measurement basis switching, which is critical for scaling up entanglement distribution protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the polarization state analyzer. The input pulse enters the circulator (CIRC) through port 1 and proceeds through port 2 into the Sagnac loop for phase mod- ulation. After propagating through the loop, the pulse re- enters port 2 of the CIRC and is routed to port 3, pass- ing through a polarization controller (PC) implementing the Hadamard operation before reaching the final polariz- ing beamsplitter (PBS). Fiber types are color-coded as blue for polarization maintaining (PM) and yellow for single-mode (SM).

FIG. 2. Schematic of the experimental setup. Polarization-entangled photon pairs are generated by a fiber-based non-degenerate source in a Sagnac-loop configuration, pumped by a 1 GHz actively mode-locked laser. The non-degenerate photons, depicted in red (signal) and blue (idler), are separated by a wavelength-division multiplexer (WDM) and sent to the Sagnac receivers (Fig. 1), labelled Alice and Bob. A system-on-chip (SoC) generates and controls the electrical pulses driving the polarization modulation, and the photons are detected using superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs). ISO: isolator, CIRC: circulator, PBC: polarizing beam combiner, PBS: polarizing beamsplitter.

FIG. 3. Visibility scans of the entangled states in the two mutual unbiased bases X and Y. These scans are obtained by modulating Alice at 0 (for X-basis) and −π/2 (for Y-basis), while Bob changes the relative phase between the receivers from 0 to π.

FIG. 4. Long-term stability of the system during a 1 GHz CHSH test driven by a 1024-bit pseudo-random sequence. The plots show the evolution over time of the S parameter (top panel) and the CHSH correlators (bottom panel).
